calendarNavigationContract.scope: Automation-only hardening after isolated BrowserStack Loyalty TC02 reproduced its four-second range-settling timeout on 13 October.
calendarNavigationContract.rangeSelection: Departure first. No return-month preflight or earlier anchor. At most two requested-departure taps with observed state transitions; assert exact requested departure and return before confirming.
calendarNavigationContract.scrollSafety: Use observed viewport/footer bounds and a measured gutter outside all visible day cells. Execute a continuous W3C touch swipe with no pre-movement hold; XCTest drag duration is a press duration, not movement time. Halve travel on each observed direction reversal, down to one eighth, within the unchanged attempt bound. Missing geometry or gutter fails without a gesture. Scrolling must preserve selection; fully contained stable enabled day cells are required for taps.
calendarNavigationContract.qualification: 13 October iPhone 17 Pro/iOS 26.5: original hold-and-drag reproduced an unintended November 8 departure locally. No-hold swipe passed TC02 calendar/fare stages; TC02 then failed on the missing insufficient-points warning. After bounded overshoot correction, cross-month TC36 passed twice consecutively (calendar-local-edit-20261013-b and -c); 470 offline/retry checks and scoped harness passed. Android/BrowserStack qualification and TC05 boundary-date requalification remain outstanding.
